text:
Vanessa Ortiz: Final sprint demo notes (Provision-to-ready automation) — dropping here so folks have the numbers + what shipped + what’s next.

**Before / after (time-to-ready)**
Baseline (last ~10 Dedicated bring-ups, from logs + ops notes):
- overall TTR p50: **~6h 20m**
- overall TTR p95: **~18h 10m**
- biggest delay contributors: imaging variability (mirror/region), manual handoffs during bootstrap, and “Ready” ambiguity (routing sometimes saw capacity too early)

Pilot runs (new pipeline, staging + 1 internal pool + 1 small customer expansion window):
- overall TTR p50: **~2h 05m**
- overall TTR p95: **~6h 40m**
- median human-touch time: **near 0** (mostly just monitoring)

Stage medians (pilot):
- Terraform / infra provision: **28–45m** (region/SKU dependent)
- Imaging (golden image + node prep): **35–70m** (still our biggest spread)
- Bootstrap (k8s + charts): **20–35m**
- Validation gates (net/GPU/smoke): **10–18m**
- Perf-canary readiness suite: **12–20m**

**What shipped (high level)**
- Provisioning state machine: `Requested → Provisioning → Imaging → Bootstrapping → Validating → Ready/Failed` w/ persisted transitions + audit trail
- Terraform orchestration wrapper w/ idempotency + sane retries
- Golden image pipeline + version pinning (runtime prereqs + drivers) + promotion steps
- Config schema validation + policy gates + admin break-glass (audited)
- Readiness gates: GPU health (ECC), networking/DNS/TLS, runtime smoke test
- Perf-canary “readiness suite” integrated as final gate
- Time-to-ready metrics (overall + per-stage) + dashboard + stuck-stage alerts (ticketing for non-page)
- Slack progress updates (stage start/finish/failure) w/ correlation IDs + links to logs/runbooks
- Control plane Ready semantics tightened: routing only advertises pools in **Ready**

**What didn’t make it / partial**
- Drift detection shipped behind flag (works for runtime settings, not fully for helm values yet)
- Allowlist/migration tooling for edge-case configs: in progress (we used break-glass + manual note for the one known edge case)

**Next up (proposed follow-ons)**
1) Imaging variability: add mirror prewarm + fallback + better detection (region/SKU)
2) Expand pilot: 2 more regions + one “spikier” SKU mix
3) Make break-glass less scary: explicit expiration + required “reason” + automatic ticket
4) Backfill historical metrics to make the before/after dashboard less hand-wavy
5) Tighten runbooks + oncall ergonomics (error strings now point to the right section, but more examples needed)

Links:
- Dashboard: https://observability.redwood.example/d/dedicated-ttr
- Confluence overview: https://confluence.redwood.example/x/provision-to-ready
- Linear project: https://linear.app/redwood/project/ENG-2741

Big thanks to everyone who jumped on the pilot hiccups quickly :pray: Please reply in-thread with: (a) anything I missed, (b) any “do NOT roll this wider until X” concerns.

Provisioning Bot: :white_check_mark: Demo artifact uploaded: `ttr-demo-2024-03-10.pdf` (internal) • Correlation example: `prov_run=prv_01HTX...` • Dashboard snapshot saved.

Irene Choi: This is awesome. The p95 drop is the headline I’m going to repeat.

Two q’s:
1) Are we confident the pilot p95 isn’t just “nice weather”? (i.e., did we hit any quota/IAM issues and still recover)
2) Can we put a stake in the ground for the SLO proposal based on these numbers (even if staged)?

Aisha Bello: Re (1) — we *did* hit one IAM permission gap in staging and one quota bump in eu-west (both are in the failure stats). The key change is they’re now clearly categorized + retried safely + surfaced early, instead of someone discovering 2–3h later.

From the dashboard:
- failed runs (pilot window): **2 / 17** (both in staging)
- auto-recovered after retry: **3 / 17** (quota throttling + transient terraform provider error)

Re (2) — my suggestion for SLO v0:
- **90%** of provisioning runs reach Ready within **8h** (pools)
- **99%** within **24h** (with documented exclusions: vendor capacity delays, procurement holds)

And then we ratchet after we have more region/SKU coverage.

Jamal Pierce: +1 on Aisha’s SLO framing. Also adding the “before” numbers in the demo were based on 10 historical bring-ups; I can expand to 25 if we want to reduce sampling bias.

One note: imaging spread is still the main driver of p95. When imaging goes long, everything else looks “fine” but the run just sits.

Harish Reddy: Operator POV from the pilot:
- CLI + bot updates were the biggest win. Not having to paste logs into 4 places saved us a ton.
- The new error messages w/ “try X / see runbook section Y” are *actually* readable.

Two pain points:
1) when we re-ran validation only, the CLI output didn’t clearly say it reused cached artifacts vs redoing things. (minor, but confusing)
2) we need a single “what do I do if Imaging > 90m” playbook. Right now it’s scattered.

Gabe Wilson: For (1) ^ we have partial stage re-run + cached artifacts in the latest PR but the CLI output is still generic. I can tweak the output to explicitly show `cache_hit=true` for stages.

For imaging > 90m: we can add detection that says “likely mirror slowness” vs “node stuck” based on progress markers + add a recommended fallback (alternate mirror or prewarm). That’s basically ENG-2757.

Victor Alvarez: Networking gate results were clean in pilot except for 1 DNS misconfig (helm values) that caused bootstrap to “succeed” but validation to fail.

I want to call out: the DNS/TLS checks caught a class of issues that previously would’ve made it to routing and then been a nightmare to debug.

Nina Petrova: Re “do NOT roll wider until X” — I’m comfortable with staged expansion, but I want us to explicitly test 2 things before we declare victory:
- heterogeneous SKUs in the same region (we have guardrails but haven’t proven we aren’t assuming too much)
- partial capacity expansions (add nodes to an existing pool) — state machine paths differ slightly

Keiko Yamamoto: On autoscaling/guardrails: we didn’t change the scaling logic (non-goal), but we *did* add region defaults and module guardrails that will prevent a couple of the historical footguns.

If we expand pilot to more regions, I’d like a quick review pass on the defaults per region so we don’t accidentally encode a wrong assumption.

Connor O'Brien: Release plan proposal:
- keep prod flag OFF by default
- enable for 1 internal pool expansion in prod next week during low-traffic window
- if success, enable for customer expansions that explicitly opt-in (CS aligned)

Rollback is straightforward: pause run + revert to legacy bring-up checklist; routing remains protected by Ready gate either way.

Kira Thompson: I’ll consolidate runbook gaps:
- add a dedicated section: “Imaging taking too long (>90m): symptoms, likely causes, steps, when to escalate”
- add “stage re-run semantics” examples (what is safe to re-run and what is not)

If folks can DM me screenshots/log snippets from the pilot that were confusing, I’ll incorporate them.

Miles Thornton: One more “don’t roll until X”: please keep an eye on metric cardinality as we add more tags (pool_id, customer, region, sku, run_id). The current safeguards look ok but we should verify in prod.

Sergio Costa: Dashboard side: I added filters for `pool_id` + `region` and a drilldown to provisioning events. If we’re going to use this in exec updates, I can add a single “headline” panel (p50/p95 last 7d, plus failure rate) so it’s not 20 graphs.

Vanessa Ortiz: Super helpful. Action items I captured:
- Gabe: improve CLI output for cache hits + stage rerun clarity
- Kira: imaging >90m playbook + rerun semantics section
- Jamal/Aisha: expand baseline dataset + propose SLO v0 in the Confluence SLO doc
- Connor: draft prod staged rollout plan w/ explicit success/rollback criteria
- Nina/Keiko: add hetero-SKU + expansion-path test cases to the pilot checklist
- Miles: prod check on metrics cardinality after first prod pool

I’ll post a short “demo recap” in #eng-platform too since Ready semantics touches routing. :thumbsup:
